articles.title: Van: Desert Scene
articles.summary: Warm orange-brown swirl pattern like marbled sand or camouflage, satin finish with a faint sparkle. Reads as a warm terracotta and rust orange with dark brown veining, like burnt sandstone or tooled leather; no dunes or cactus, just a busy earthy marble.
articles.what: Airbrushed dunes with a saguaro in the middle distance, always. Up close: Sandy orange-tan ground with a rough fibrous grit, crossed by wobbly dark-brown contour lines 4-8 px thick that loop round blobby islands and little pits, like cracked clay, wood burl or a topographic map. Lines run in parallel pairs and wander in all directions. From a distance: Reads as a warm terracotta and rust orange with dark brown veining, like burnt sandstone or tooled leather; no dunes or cactus, just a busy earthy marble. Measured spec (average): metal 4, roughness 103, coat 90. Shine: satin. Metal: none. It brings its own colours.
when: Best on: body, sides, hero panel.
Fits: truck / off-road, show car, stock car.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Van: Desert Scene" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Leave BASE COLOR on Use finish's own color to keep its colours.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Doors, hood and roof: wide panels show the contour lines
Lower body and tailgate for a rugged look
Cream, white or black numbers over a plate read; orange and brown numbers vanish into the veining.
Bold stripes and big blocks: the veining is busy, so solid heavy graphics read on top
Pairs well with: cream, brown, matte black, chrome.
pitfalls: Not an airbrushed dune scene with a saguaro: no scene, sky or cactus in the render, despite the name
Not metallic or glittery: metal is none
Avoid: small numbers, next to other busy patterns.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 4 (non-metal paint), roughness 103 (satin or eggshell), clearcoat 90 (satin or weak clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: roughness and clearcoat vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: small numbers, next to other busy patterns.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: bold stripes and big blocks: the veining is busy, so solid heavy graphics read on top; cream or black lettering: legible when on a plate
Patterns to avoid: marble, wave, topographic or noise patterns: duplicate the contour lines and clutter
Spec overlays that work: gloss clear: lacquered leather or burl look; matte-gloss split: panel structure
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.

articles.title: Disco: Discotheque Haze
articles.summary: Soft dark teal satin haze, mottled and cloudy like smoke holding a light beam. Reads as a dark teal-green with a frosty speckle, like mossy rock or smoke on a cold lake; moody and calm.
articles.what: Dry ice and cigarette smoke holding the beams up where you can see them. Up close: Teal field of fine rough granite-like mottling: deep green-blue with darker blotches and scattered pale frosty patches 5-30 px, like lichen on stone or frozen mist. Grainy and uneven, with no lines or shapes. From a distance: Reads as a dark teal-green with a frosty speckle, like mossy rock or smoke on a cold lake; moody and calm. Measured spec (average): metal 0, roughness 90, coat 74. Shine: satin. Metal: none. It brings its own colours.
when: Fits: gt / sports car, show car, open wheel.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Disco: Discotheque Haze" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Leave BASE COLOR on Use finish's own color to keep its colours.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Body sides and roof: wide calm panels show the haze
Hood: even grain avoids a heavy look
White, silver or yellow numbers read; teal or dark ones vanish.
Wide black, silver or white stripes: clean contrast on teal
Pairs well with: black, silver, white, chrome.
pitfalls: Not metallic: metal is zero, and there is no sparkle
Not smooth haze: grain is rough and rocky
Avoid: big dark areas in the sim, next to other loud finishes.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 0 (non-metal paint), roughness 90 (satin gloss), clearcoat 74 (satin or weak clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: roughness and clearcoat vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: big dark areas in the sim, next to other loud finishes.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: wide black, silver or white stripes: clean contrast on teal; thin chrome pinlines: crisp edge on the rough grain
Patterns to avoid: other mottled, camo or smoke patterns: mush
Spec overlays that work: gloss clearcoat: deepens the teal like wet stone; fine flake: adds the nightclub glint missing here
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.

articles.title: Van: Eagle Gold
articles.summary: Dark olive-gold micro-flake with a mirror shine, like burnished gold leaf with black outlines. A dark-gold and black zebra-like stripe field, a glowing gold leaf with black veining; reads rich and busy with cloudy darker areas.
articles.what: Gold leaf laid over size and burnished, then outlined in black. Up close: Tight flowing wavy lines, 3-6 px, in bright gold and black, running diagonally top-right to bottom-left like feather barbs or zebra fur. The gold carries a fine hammered leaf grain, and broad dark brown patches drift under the lines. From a distance: A dark-gold and black zebra-like stripe field, a glowing gold leaf with black veining; reads rich and busy with cloudy darker areas. Measured spec (average): metal 236, roughness 24, coat 55. Shine: mirror. Metal: full. It brings its own colours.
when: Best on: body, trim, hero panel.
Fits: show car, gt / sports car, stock car.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Van: Eagle Gold" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Leave BASE COLOR on Use finish's own color to keep its colours.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Hood, roof and doors: strong when wide panels show the flow
Avoid next to bright chrome trim
Black numbers lose to the black lines; use a solid black or white plate with a bright outline.
None or plain black stripes: the pinline pattern is already full
Pairs well with: black, deep red, cream, chrome.
pitfalls: Not plain gold chrome: the black lines cover about a third of the surface
Not tiger stripe camo: it is fine gold feather barbs, not wide bands
Avoid: large dark areas in the sim, next to bright chrome.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 236 (true metallic), roughness 24 (wet mirror gloss), clearcoat 55 (strong-to-medium clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: clearcoat vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: large dark areas in the sim, next to bright chrome.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: none or plain black stripes: the pinline pattern is already full; a clean black panel or number plate: calm area
Patterns to avoid: other stripe, animal print or wave patterns: moire against the lines; fine flake or grain: noise on lines
Spec overlays that work: gloss clearcoat sheet: deepens the mirror gold; matte clearcoat band for a contrast trim: dull accents next to the gold
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.

articles.title: Van: Flame Job
articles.summary: Warm orange-brown granular horizontal bands, stippled and streaky, satin sheen with faint glints, no clear flame shapes. Reads as a busy burnt-orange and brown wood-grain or rust-sunset surface with a horizontal streak; it is warm but dark overall.
articles.what: Licks laid out in tape, shot hot in the middle and cool at the tips. Up close: Warm marbled field of squiggly amber, gold and dark-brown veins that stack into loose horizontal bands. Hot yellow-orange blobs sit between near-black brown outlines, like molten crust or burnt toffee. No readable flame tongues at this size. From a distance: Reads as a busy burnt-orange and brown wood-grain or rust-sunset surface with a horizontal streak; it is warm but dark overall. Measured spec (average): metal 48, roughness 100, coat 114. Shine: satin. Metal: low. It brings its own colours.
when: Fits: stock car, dirt late model, truck / off-road.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Van: Flame Job" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Leave BASE COLOR on Use finish's own color to keep its colours.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Body sides: horizontal bands run with the car's length
Hood: the fiery colours draw the eye
Dark brown veins swallow numbers; use cream or white with black outline on a solid plate.
Wide horizontal stripes in cream or black: fit the banded direction
Pairs well with: black, cream, chrome, dark brown.
pitfalls: Not a flame livery: no pointed tongues or clear flame shapes
Not plain orange: it is dark brown and gold mixed
Avoid: numbers over the busy bands, large dark areas that swallow the warm tones.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 48 (low metal, like carbon or subtle flake), roughness 100 (satin or eggshell), clearcoat 114 (satin or weak clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: metal and roughness and clearcoat vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: numbers over the busy bands, large dark areas that swallow the warm tones.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: wide horizontal stripes in cream or black: fit the banded direction; outlined lettering or a number plate: needed to stay legible
Patterns to avoid: other organic marbling or camo: both are blotchy and merge into mud
Spec overlays that work: gloss clearcoat: deepens the amber like varnish; soft sparkle flake: already present, do not add much more
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.

articles.title: Shag: Fondue Copper
articles.summary: Hammered copper micro-flake, glossy warm orange metal, fine dense sparkle, bright and reflective. Reads as warm worn copper with a pitted, peppered look; the dots become a dense dark speckle on bright orange-brown metal.
articles.what: Hammered copper on the good pot, brought out for guests four times a year. Up close: Burnt-orange copper field with blocky patchy tone shifts, covered in small round pits and dimples, each a dark centre ringed by a bright golden rim. Sizes vary from tiny dots to bigger craters, scattered randomly like a hammered pot. From a distance: Reads as warm worn copper with a pitted, peppered look; the dots become a dense dark speckle on bright orange-brown metal. Measured spec (average): metal 188, roughness 45, coat 72. Shine: gloss. Metal: high. It brings its own colours.
when: Best on: body, hero panel, trim.
Fits: show car, gt / sports car, stock car.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Shag: Fondue Copper" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Leave BASE COLOR on Use finish's own color to keep its colours.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Hood and roof: pits read as texture on big flats
Side panels for a full hero look
Black or cream numbers with an outline read; orange or brown numbers vanish and the pits break up thin strokes.
Black or cream stripes and block graphics: contrast on the warm copper
Pairs well with: black, cream, deep teal, chrome.
pitfalls: Not fine metallic flake: the features are round dimples with dark centres, not glitter
Not plain copper gloss: the surface is pitted and patchy
Avoid: clashes with red-orange neighbours, glare hides fine numbers.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 188 (true metallic), roughness 45 (high gloss), clearcoat 72 (satin or weak clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: metal and roughness and clearcoat vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: clashes with red-orange neighbours, glare hides fine numbers.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: black or cream stripes and block graphics: contrast on the warm copper; deep teal accents: complementary colour to copper
Patterns to avoid: fine glitter or other flake overlays: the dimples already supply sparkle; other hammered or pitted textures: doubles up
Spec overlays that work: gloss/matte stripe bands: wet bands against the pitted metal; brushed or grain spec in one direction: contrasts the random pits
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.
